edges.description: Inferred from the activity of wild-type HECTD4 in cancer cells and cultured nerve cells; substrate ubiquitination has not been measured in patient cells.
No HECTD4 substrate has been tied to callosal axon growth or midline crossing; the link rests on the human genetics and on the wider association of E3 ligase genes with neurodevelopmental syndromes.
The intermediate steps between reduced HECTD4 ubiquitination and the neurodevelopmental phenotype are unknown.

nodes.description: Biallelic HECTD4 variants remove or reduce HECTD4 function. Patient RNA studies support a loss-of-function effect for the truncating alleles; the compound heterozygous missense alleles are presumed loss of function on in silico grounds. HECTD4 is a HECT-family E3 ligase whose catalytic HECT domain accepts ubiquitin from an E2 enzyme and transfers it to substrates.

nodes.description: HECTD4 interacts with the NMDA receptor subunit GluN2B, an interaction that weakens in a rat ischemic stroke model, and in cultured nerve cells HECTD4 knockdown increases GluN2B phosphorylation and intracellular calcium after hypoxic or NMDA challenge, partly through stabilized MALT1 and degradation of the phosphatase STEP61. Whether the same occurs in the developing brain, and whether it lowers seizure threshold in patients, has not been studied, so this node has no downstream edge.

evidence.reference_title: The Weakened Interaction Between HECTD4 and GluN2B in Ischemic Stroke Promotes Calcium Overload and Brain Injury Through a Mechanism Involving the Decrease of GluN2B and MALT1 Ubiquitination.
evidence.snippet: we conclude that the downregulation of HECTD4 in ischemic stroke rat brain accounts for calcium overload and brain injury due to activating GluN2B directly and indirectly through a mechanism involving the reduced ubiquitination of GluN2B and MALT1, respectively.

nodes.description: Loss of HECTD4 is expected to stabilize its substrates. In breast cancer cells HECTD4 depletion raises COX-2 and HECTD4 also targets its regulatory kinase MKK7; in cultured nerve cells under hypoxic or NMDA injury HECTD4 knockdown lowers ubiquitination of the NMDA receptor subunit GluN2B and of MALT1. Which substrates matter in the developing human brain is not known.
